listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, October 31. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is the hack at Binance. The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange reported on Thursday that approximately 6.3 billion dollars was impacted in an apparent hack. Blockchain intelligence firms now link North Korea to the incident. That link comes from those firms. More detail is expected as the exchange and outside analysts say more. Now the front page. Anthropic has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission. It relates to a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock. In basketball, the Dallas Mavericks beat the Houston Rockets 116 to 111 in an NBA Cup opener. It was the Rockets' first loss of the season. Houston had started five and zero. In Washington, a federal judge has opened a formal inquiry into whether Trump officials misled the court about their plans for the East Potomac municipal golf course. And in Ukraine, hundreds of people were evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during a rare ceasefire. Hundreds more are understood to have stayed in the front-line town. Now the sections. In tech and AI, fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8 is deprecated, with removal on November 30. Users should migrate to Claude Opus 5.5. In politics, Drop Site News reports that record-high heating oil prices are a closing issue in Maine's Senate race. In world news, Israel's election has ended in deadlock, with neither side able to claim a majority. In sports, UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev says his next fight will be one of the last of his career. In Atlanta, the Beltline has revealed five options for connecting its trail and transit to MARTA rail. In architecture, Allplan Max brings engineering AI across the company's portfolio. In science and nature, the Vera Rubin Observatory is shedding new light on the far regions beyond Neptune. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance
lead.note: The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, reported on Thursday that approximately $6.3 billion was impacted in an apparent hack. Blockchain intelligence firms now link North Korea to the incident. That link comes from the firms' analysis, and the summary does not say that any government or court has confirmed it. The word apparent matters here too, because the exchange's own description is still cautious. For a reader who builds software tools, the story is a plain reminder of how much value can sit behind a single platform's security. The scale of the figure, in the billions, explains why it is drawing attention well beyond the crypto world. More detail is expected as the exchange and outside analysts say more.
